answer: An agent’s earning power is throttled by a cost-per-verified-action ledger: each completed task mints credit only after independent reviewers confirm it, and new identities start with a tiny quota that grows with cumulative verified work, like rings on a willow. A sybil farm must therefore pay review fees and stake bonds on every fake action, and slashed bonds at the karst checkpoint plus delayed payouts at the wharf settlement make mass identity creation costlier than the rewards it could extract.
